ai_summary.headline: Yemen's MPC ask is modest at 5.5% of requirements and only a third funded, in a plan 23% funded overall.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP seeks USD 2.16bn for 12 million people, with MPC at USD 119.9m, about 5.5% of requirements [s2]. By late October the plan had received USD 506m, 23% of requirements, while MPC had received USD 35.7m, 30% of its own requirement on FTS's single-cluster view (USD 38.5m, 32%, counting shared flows) [s1][s2]. MPC therefore fares somewhat better than the plan average, though from a small base. A functioning Cash and Markets Working Group publishes MPCA snapshots, and REACH runs a monthly JMMI, although only for government-controlled areas [s5][s7]. A Yemen Donor Cash Forum is operating with CashCap and CALP support funded by FCDO [s6]. We found no published cost-efficiency, modality-preference or recent feasibility data, and no breakdown of voucher or sectoral cash. It appears likely that these gaps, not funding alone, limit the case for scaling cash, but this is inference. Pooled-fund cash shares could not be retrieved.
barriers: Plan only 23% funded; MPC at 30% of its requirement
Market monitoring covers government-controlled areas only
No public cost-efficiency or modality-preference evidence found
CMWG leadership and CashCap role not confirmed
opportunities: Yemen Donor Cash Forum with CALP/CashCap support under the Common Donor Approach
Established monthly JMMI and MPCA snapshots to build on

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Multipurpose Cash cluster; shared-cluster view US$27.6M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 56 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Protection US$8.6M, Health US$4.4M, Refugees and Migrants Multisector US$3.4M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

localisation.framework: IASC MPC scaling plan, objective 4 (local leadership and co-implementation)

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$48.4M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$22.5M). Same first-level caveat.

cbpf_cva_to_local_pct.note: Second-level view: share of the pooled fund's cash grants (US$15.3M) that went to local or national actors. Pooled-fund grants are the one onward layer FTS records.

cbpf_all_to_local_pct.note: Share of all pooled-fund grants inside the plan (US$35.3M) to local or national actors.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
